findings.failure_scenario: The RO_RUN_RW_ESCAPE check only looks at --rw paths inside DIR. `ro-run.py --protect /w --rw /w -- cmd` passes, because the path is inside-or-equal and not a symlink. `--protect /w --rw /home/u` (an ancestor) passes unchecked. Either way the whole protected tree becomes writable with exit 0, although --protect is meant to be fail-closed (D11). The shipped catalog entries cannot reach this. The runtime --rw addition in roles.py:381 only targets the executor, which has no --protect. A future caller or hand-written argv can.
findings.reproduction: Read-only analysis of _protect: for --rw equal to DIR, `_inside(absolute, directory)` is true, lstat is not a symlink and `_inside(real, resolved)` is true, so no error. For an ancestor, none of the three `_inside` tests is true, so the loop does nothing.

triage_reproduction.cmd: W=$(mktemp -d -p $PWD .tri-XXXX); python3 -I packages/orch/scripts/ro-run.py --protect $W --rw $W -- true; python3 -I packages/orch/scripts/ro-run.py --protect $W --rw $PWD -- true
triage_reproduction.observed: Both calls exit 0 with no RO_RUN_RW_ESCAPE; the protected tree is granted writable.

findings.failure_scenario: The overlap check only tests whether DIR is inside a default writable root. It does not test whether a default root resolves inside DIR. With HOME inside the checkout (or ~/.grok a symlink into it), `<checkout>/.grok` stays writable under --protect. A protected role can then write files into the checkout, including Grok's own config directory.
findings.reproduction: Read-only analysis. HOME=<DIR> makes roots[3]=<DIR>/.grok. `_inside(<DIR>, <DIR>/.grok)` is false, so there is no refusal, and the realpath'd root stays in `writable`.

triage_reproduction.observed: exit 0; the default root $W/.grok resolves inside the protected DIR and stays writable.

findings.failure_scenario: ProtectedRunTests.setUp creates its checkout in `SCRIPT.parents[3]`, assumed to be the repo root. If the repo sits under /tmp, /var/tmp or ~/.grok, the probe exits 3 with RO_RUN_PROTECT_OVERLAP. setUp only skips on LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE and ABI_TOO_OLD, so the next assertEqual fails instead of skipping. In an own-repo layout (module split) parents[3] is no longer the repo root. A killed run also leaves `.ro-run-test-*` in the repo root. The guidance suggested a directory under ~/.cache.
findings.reproduction: Run the test from a checkout located under /tmp.

triage_reproduction.cmd: python3 -I packages/orch/scripts/ro-run.py --protect $TMPDIR -- true  (stands in for a repo under /tmp); sed -n 108,120p packages/orch/tests/test_ro_run.py
triage_reproduction.observed: RO_RUN_PROTECT_OVERLAP with exit 3; the setUp skip condition covers only LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE and LANDLOCK_ABI_TOO_OLD, so the next assertEqual fails instead of skipping.

findings.failure_scenario: test_without_a_project_the_run_is_refused_with_the_flag_named now patches the private `aicore.state.locations._marker_found` to False and blanks the SKM_* env vars. This is unrelated to Grok launch. It hides the environment condition that made the test fail on the executor's host (an ancestor of /tmp carries a project marker) and couples the test to a private aicore function.
findings.reproduction: git diff packages/orch/tests/test_conductor.py, hunk at ProjectContextTests.

findings.failure_scenario: On a kernel without Landlock, the syscall returns -1. With --protect the user sees `LANDLOCK_ABI_TOO_OLD: -1` and never gets LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE with the errno text. The same Landlock-less kernel without --protect still reports LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE. The contract says ABI < 3, so this is defensible. The message is misleading.
findings.reproduction: Read-only analysis: the `protected and abi < 3` branch precedes the `abi < 1` branch.

triage_reproduction.cmd: python3 -I with ro-run.py loaded as a module and _landlock_abi patched to -1; m.restrict([], ['/x'])
triage_reproduction.observed: prints LANDLOCK_ABI_TOO_OLD: -1 instead of LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE with the errno text.

findings.failure_scenario: test_no_protect_preserves_default_writes_and_symlink_grants sits in ProtectedRunTests, whose setUp skips on ABI < 3. The 'behaviour without --protect is unchanged' check therefore disappears on ABI 1/2 kernels, where it is most relevant. It also never asserts that the default-root write file exists.
findings.reproduction: Read-only analysis of setUp's skipTest condition.

triage_reproduction.observed: setUp calls skipTest on LANDLOCK_ABI_TOO_OLD for the whole class, which includes test_no_protect_preserves_default_writes_and_symlink_grants; that test never asserts the default-root file exists.

rejected.reason: The _marker_found patch is test isolation inside the write set. It is not a Grok launch defect and breaks no acceptance command or stated rule. The finding gives no failing scenario, only coupling to a private aicore function. Not a Blocker or Major.
